title: Chicken Liver Pâté
subtitle: Smooth, buttery pâté with brandy and thyme
excerpt: Chicken livers fried briefly with shallot, garlic, thyme, and brandy, blended until silky smooth with plenty of butter. Sealed with clarified butter and chilled. Serve with toast and cornichons.

recipe.sourceNotes: Smooth chicken liver pâté is a French classic, though it was adopted enthusiastically into British cooking in the 20th century, where it became a standard dinner party starter and sandwich filling. The key technique is cooking the livers only until they are just pink inside: overcooked liver becomes grainy and bitter. The butter must be generous: it provides both the silky texture and the flavour that makes a good pâté. Sealing with clarified butter prevents oxidation and extends the fridge life to up to a week.

recipeTools.notes: And a food processor or stick blender.

content.text: Cook the livers over high heat for 2 minutes per side only: they should still be pink in the centre when you remove them from the heat. They will continue to cook in the residual heat of the pan. Blending while still warm gives the smoothest result. Pass through a sieve after blending if you want an exceptionally smooth pâté.
Heat the oil and 20 g of the 150 g butter in a frying pan over medium heat. Soften the shallot for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and thyme leaves. Cook for 1 minute.
Increase to high heat. Add the livers in a single layer. Cook for 2 minutes per side until browned outside but still pink inside. Pour in the brandy and let it sizzle for 30 seconds. Season.
Tip the livers and all the pan juices into a food processor. Add the remaining cold butter and the cream. Blend until completely smooth. Check seasoning. Pour into ramekins or a terrine dish.

Melt the 80 g butter for the seal over low heat. Skim the foam from the surface and pour the clear butter over the pâté, leaving the white solids in the pan. Leave to set. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Serve with toasted bread and cornichons.
